## First Pass

Do this before writing a situation code.

If you cannot work the full table, use the panic fork in `00_READ_THIS_FIRST.md`: outside/on foot, vehicle, building, hurt/sick, leaving/returning/sheltering, or conflicting/unsafe instructions.

## Precedence Snapshot

- Direct physical danger comes first.
- If the advised shelter becomes dangerous, move to the nearest safer version of the same protection goal.
- Tornado shelter-now wins during active tornado danger unless the shelter itself is flooding, electrified, collapsing, on fire, full of gas/CO, or otherwise immediately unsafe.
- Floodwater blocks movement, re-entry, documentation, route planning, and shelter use until a safer dry option or official route exists.
- Fire, gas, CO, collapse, downed lines, or life-threatening injury can override a generic shelter/stay plan.
- Chemical/hazmat and radiation/nuclear current local orders control unless the shelter or route itself has immediate visible danger.
- Card 13 is for reliability failure, not ordinary biological/pandemic, public-health, or hazard routing.

| Order | Check | First routing |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Active kill zone | Move away from fire, smoke, collapse, floodwater, traffic, violence, severe weather, hazardous material, active shaking/aftershock, damaged building, tornado/severe wind, hurricane/storm-surge danger, tsunami/coastal warning danger, lightning/thunderstorm exposure, chemical release, radiation/fallout warning, or any immediate threat. Route flood danger to `hazard_cards/01_FLOOD.md`; route wildfire smoke or active wildfire danger to `hazard_cards/04_WILDFIRE_SMOKE.md`; route earthquake shaking, aftershock, damaged structure, or trapped-person danger to `hazard_cards/05_EARTHQUAKE.md`; route tsunami natural warning signs, official tsunami alert, beach/harbor/waterway danger, or tsunami re-entry conflict to `hazard_cards/11_TSUNAMI_COASTAL.md`; route tornado warning/signs, severe wind, mobile-home/vehicle/outside exposure, or downed-line danger to `hazard_cards/06_TORNADO_SEVERE_WIND.md`; route hurricane/tropical-storm alerts, storm surge, official evacuation/shelter order, or hurricane re-entry conflict to `hazard_cards/10_HURRICANE.md`; route thunder, visible lightning, unsafe outdoor/open-water exposure, or lightning-strike injury to `hazard_cards/09_LIGHTNING.md`; route chemical/hazmat alerts, suspected release, exposure, or shelter/evacuation conflict to `hazard_cards/07_CHEMICAL_HAZMAT.md`; route radiation/nuclear alerts, fallout warnings, radiological contamination, or KI rumors to `hazard_cards/08_RADIATION_NUCLEAR.md`; route personal danger to `09_PROTECT_YOURSELF.md`. |
| 2 | Life-threatening injury or severe/worsening illness | Look for severe bleeding, blocked breathing, major burns, shock, inability to move safely, severe/worsening illness, or a high-risk sick person. Route to `07_FIRST_AID_AND_HEALTH_CONTINUITY.md`. If contagious-disease instructions, exposure, sick household/group, shelter outbreak, facility crowding, or epidemic/pandemic risk affects movement or shelter, also route to `hazard_cards/12_BIOLOGICAL_PANDEMIC_CONTAGIOUS_DISEASE.md`. |
| 3 | Fire, smoke, gas, electric, fuel, generator, CO, or downed-line hazard | Leave or avoid the hazard first. Do not repair utilities. Route building/utility smoke to `06_FIRE_POWER_UTILITIES_CO.md`; route wildfire smoke/air-quality danger to `hazard_cards/04_WILDFIRE_SMOKE.md`; route earthquake-related gas, fire, downed-line, damaged-utility, and CO overlap to `hazard_cards/05_EARTHQUAKE.md` and `06_FIRE_POWER_UTILITIES_CO.md`; route tsunami floodwater, damaged-utility, downed-line, gas/fire/CO, wet-electrical, or re-entry utility overlap to `hazard_cards/11_TSUNAMI_COASTAL.md` and `06_FIRE_POWER_UTILITIES_CO.md`; route tornado/severe-wind downed-line, damaged-utility, gas/fire/CO, and outage overlap to `hazard_cards/06_TORNADO_SEVERE_WIND.md` and `06_FIRE_POWER_UTILITIES_CO.md`; route hurricane outage, generator/CO, downed-line, gas/fire, wet-electrical, or re-entry utility overlap to `hazard_cards/10_HURRICANE.md` and `06_FIRE_POWER_UTILITIES_CO.md`; route lightning/thunderstorm downed-line, outage, indoor electrical/plumbing caution, or strike-injury overlap to `hazard_cards/09_LIGHTNING.md` and `06_FIRE_POWER_UTILITIES_CO.md`; route chemical/hazmat fire, smoke, gas, CO, or utility overlap to `hazard_cards/07_CHEMICAL_HAZMAT.md` and `06_FIRE_POWER_UTILITIES_CO.md`; route radiation/nuclear shelter conflicts with fire, gas, CO, collapse, or utility danger to `hazard_cards/08_RADIATION_NUCLEAR.md` plus `06_FIRE_POWER_UTILITIES_CO.md`. |
| 4 | Exposure | Check heat, cold, wet, wind, desert, open water, altitude, contaminated air, smoke, earthquake damage, tsunami/coastal danger, tornado/severe wind, hurricane/storm surge, thunder/lightning, chemical exposure, radiation/fallout warning, or lack of shelter. Route heat danger to `hazard_cards/02_HEAT.md`; route cold danger to `hazard_cards/03_COLD.md`; route wildfire smoke to `hazard_cards/04_WILDFIRE_SMOKE.md`; route earthquake damage/aftershock exposure to `hazard_cards/05_EARTHQUAKE.md`; route tsunami natural warning, official alert, high/inland movement, beach/harbor/waterway danger, floodwater, and re-entry decisions to `hazard_cards/11_TSUNAMI_COASTAL.md`; route tornado/severe wind shelter decisions to `hazard_cards/06_TORNADO_SEVERE_WIND.md`; route hurricane evacuation/stay, storm surge, flood/wind, outage, and re-entry decisions to `hazard_cards/10_HURRICANE.md`; route lightning safe-shelter decisions, outdoor/open-water exposure, and 30-minute wait boundary to `hazard_cards/09_LIGHTNING.md`; route chemical/hazmat exposure or shelter/evacuation conflict to `hazard_cards/07_CHEMICAL_HAZMAT.md`; route radiation/nuclear get-inside/stay-inside decisions, possible contamination, or KI rumors to `hazard_cards/08_RADIATION_NUCLEAR.md`; route general exposure to `08_EXPOSURE_SHELTER_WEATHER_MOVEMENT.md`. |
| 5 | Safe water | Identify what water is safe now. Prefer sealed bottled water when available. Route tsunami/floodwater contamination to `hazard_cards/11_TSUNAMI_COASTAL.md` and `hazard_cards/01_FLOOD.md`; route possible radiological contamination to `hazard_cards/08_RADIATION_NUCLEAR.md`; route other water minimums to `05_WATER_HYGIENE_FOOD_MINIMUMS.md`. |
| 6 | Hygiene, sanitation, and food | Keep waste, floodwater, animals, fuel, chemicals, and possible radioactive contamination away from hands, food, and water. Do not eat spoiled, flood-contaminated, chemically contaminated, or uncovered outdoor food after a radiological warning. Route active tsunami or flood contamination to `hazard_cards/11_TSUNAMI_COASTAL.md` and `hazard_cards/01_FLOOD.md`; route possible chemical contamination to `hazard_cards/07_CHEMICAL_HAZMAT.md`; route possible radiological contamination to `hazard_cards/08_RADIATION_NUCLEAR.md`. |
| 7 | Stay, shelter, move, or evacuate | Follow current, local, specific, verifiable official instructions when available. If no instructions exist, choose the option that gets you away from the most immediate threat. If instructions are stale, conflicting, impersonated, impossible, or visibly unsafe, route visible physical danger first and use `hazard_cards/13_CONFLICTING_UNRELIABLE_INSTRUCTIONS.md`. Route tsunami natural-warning, official-warning, advisory, watch, high/inland movement, and all-clear decisions to `hazard_cards/11_TSUNAMI_COASTAL.md`; route tornado/severe-wind shelter-now decisions to `hazard_cards/06_TORNADO_SEVERE_WIND.md`; route hurricane evacuation/stay and storm-surge shelter conflicts to `hazard_cards/10_HURRICANE.md`; route lightning safe-shelter and outdoor/water movement decisions to `hazard_cards/09_LIGHTNING.md`; route chemical/hazmat shelter-in-place or evacuation decisions to `hazard_cards/07_CHEMICAL_HAZMAT.md`; route radiation/nuclear get-inside/stay-inside/evacuate/all-clear decisions to `hazard_cards/08_RADIATION_NUCLEAR.md`; route public-health instructions, sick/exposed people, contagious-disease crowding, and epidemic/pandemic shelter decisions to `hazard_cards/12_BIOLOGICAL_PANDEMIC_CONTAGIOUS_DISEASE.md`; route general shelter/movement to `08_EXPOSURE_SHELTER_WEATHER_MOVEMENT.md`. |
| 8 | Shock, panic, group stress, or unsafe conflict | Make the scene safer, reduce stimulation, assign simple roles if useful, and escalate threats or severe distress. Route to `10_PSYCHOLOGICAL_FIRST_AID_GROUP_STRESS.md` and `09_PROTECT_YOURSELF.md`. |
| 9 | Alerts and communication | Get official warnings if available. Tell a contact where you are if you can do so safely. Save battery. Route to `12_COMMUNICATION_ALERTS_RECORDS_NAVIGATION.md`. |
| 10 | Help endpoint unavailable | If 911, Poison Control, hospital/clinic, pharmacy, public-health line, dialysis/device support, shelter medical desk, charging/cooling location, official route, or trained help is unavailable, unreachable, overloaded, impossible, or unsafe, route immediate life threats and active hazards first. Use `12_COMMUNICATION_ALERTS_RECORDS_NAVIGATION.md` for short location/condition/need messages and alternate channels, `07_FIRST_AID_AND_HEALTH_CONTINUITY.md` for medicines/devices/dependencies, `08_EXPOSURE_SHELTER_WEATHER_MOVEMENT.md` when safer movement toward reachable care is the issue, and `hazard_cards/13_CONFLICTING_UNRELIABLE_INSTRUCTIONS.md` when reliability or impersonation is the issue. Do not improvise medical, repair, rescue, structural, chemical, or radiation procedures from this volume. |
| 11 | Vulnerable people and separated group members | Account for children, disabled people, older adults, pregnancy/postpartum needs, medicines, medical devices, service animals, pets, and missing people. Route to `07_FIRST_AID_AND_HEALTH_CONTINUITY.md`. |
| 12 | Re-entry or return after evacuation | Do not return before officials say it is safe. If a return or all-clear message is stale, conflicting, impersonated, impossible, or visibly unsafe, use `hazard_cards/13_CONFLICTING_UNRELIABLE_INSTRUCTIONS.md`. Check from outside for obvious fire, smoke, ash, gas, electrical, flood, structural, chemical, radiation/contamination, animal, aftershock, downed-line, tsunami/coastal flood damage, hurricane/storm damage, lightning/thunderstorm, debris, or conflict hazards. Route flood return to `hazard_cards/01_FLOOD.md`; route wildfire/smoke/ash return to `hazard_cards/04_WILDFIRE_SMOKE.md`; route earthquake-damaged return to `hazard_cards/05_EARTHQUAKE.md`; route tsunami return, coastal floodwater, damaged buildings, beach/harbor/waterway danger, utility damage, or official all-clear uncertainty to `hazard_cards/11_TSUNAMI_COASTAL.md`; route tornado/severe-wind return to `hazard_cards/06_TORNADO_SEVERE_WIND.md`; route hurricane re-entry, storm surge/flood, wind damage, outage, or cleanup pressure to `hazard_cards/10_HURRICANE.md`; route thunder/lightning, storm-related downed lines, or outdoor documentation/cleanup timing to `hazard_cards/09_LIGHTNING.md`; route chemical/hazmat return, odor, unknown powder/liquid, or contaminated belongings to `hazard_cards/07_CHEMICAL_HAZMAT.md`; route radiation/nuclear all-clear, radiological contamination, KI rumor, or radioactive waste/belongings to `hazard_cards/08_RADIATION_NUCLEAR.md`; then use `11_CLEANUP_REENTRY_EARLY_RECOVERY.md`. |
| 13 | Situation code | Now write `R-D-E` and identify the tier. |

## Hard Stops

Stop reading this checklist and act if:

- you are in fire, smoke, suspected gas, carbon monoxide, floodwater, collapse risk, traffic, active violence, or severe exposure;
- someone has life-threatening injury;
- an evacuation or shelter order applies to you;
- wildfire smoke, ash, poor visibility, or air quality is threatening breathing, movement, or a high-risk person;
- earthquake shaking, aftershock, damaged building, gas smell/hissing, downed line, trapped person, or tsunami warning/sign is present;
- tsunami natural warning signs, official tsunami warning, tsunami advisory near water, beach/harbor/waterway danger, or official tsunami return restriction is present;
- tornado warning, tornado signs, severe wind, unsafe shelter, mobile-home/vehicle/outside exposure, downed line, damaged building, or trapped person is present;
- hurricane evacuation order, storm surge warning, hurricane/tropical-storm warning, extreme wind warning, flooded route, or official re-entry restriction is present;
- thunder, visible lightning, thunderstorm warning, unsafe outdoor or open-water exposure, lightning strike injury, or storm-related downed line is present;
- chemical/hazmat alert, suspected release, exposure symptoms, unknown powder/liquid, chemical odor, contaminated food/water/wound, or official chemical shelter/evacuation instruction is present;
- radiation/nuclear alert, fallout warning, radiological contamination warning, official get-inside/stay-inside/evacuation/all-clear instruction, or KI rumor is present;
- contagious-disease public-health instructions, severe/worsening illness, a high-risk sick person, unsafe shelter/facility crowding, or a shelter/facility outbreak is affecting movement, shelter, or care;
- water, food, or shelter decisions affect an infant, a medically fragile person, or a power-dependent medical device;
- heat, cold, wet clothing, failed heating/cooling, or unsafe shelter is already affecting vulnerable people;
- someone may harm themselves or others, is missing, or cannot stay safe without immediate help.

## Utility And Generator Warning

Do not reconnect utilities yourself after a fire or disaster. Do not use a generator indoors, in a garage, near doors/windows, or where exhaust can enter shelter. Do not use an oven or gas stovetop as heat.

## Water And Food Warning

Boiling or disinfecting water does not fix fuel, toxic chemical, or radioactive contamination. Never taste food to decide whether it is safe.

## Next

If the immediate danger pass is complete, go to `02_SITUATION_CODE_RDE.md`.

hard_stops.rule: Do not route to non-reviewed procedural claims.

# Hazard Card 12: Biological / Pandemic / Contagious Disease

Status: reader-facing routing card for Volume 1. This is not a diagnosis, treatment, testing, vaccine-schedule, quarantine-law, enforcement, infection-control, HVAC, or public-health-policy manual.

Source trace: `notes/source_reviews/volume01/hazard_biological_pandemic.md`
Related source trace: `notes/source_reviews/volume01/hazard_conflicting_unreliable_instructions.md`

## Use This Card When

- Public health, healthcare, school, workplace, shelter, facility, or local officials issue contagious-disease instructions.
- Someone in the household, group, shelter, facility, or aid line is sick, exposed, or at higher risk from respiratory illness.
- Crowding, shared air, shared sanitation, food/water access, medicine/device continuity, or shelter movement changes disease risk.
- Disease rumors, false all-clears, impersonated helpers, or conflicting public-health messages affect safety decisions.

## Immediate Rule

Follow current, local, specific, verifiable public-health and healthcare instructions by default. If someone is severely ill, worsening, or higher risk, route healthcare access early instead of trying to identify the disease yourself.

When public-health instructions are missing, stale, conflicting, impersonated, impossible, or visibly unsafe, route direct life safety first and use `hazard_cards/13_CONFLICTING_UNRELIABLE_INSTRUCTIONS.md` as the reliability fallback. Do not use uncertainty as a reason to ignore current credible public-health guidance.

## First Pass Checklist

Ask these in order:

1. Is anyone severely ill, worsening, unable to breathe normally, unable to stay awake, dehydrated, injured, pregnant, very young, older, disabled, immunocompromised, medically fragile, or dependent on medicines/devices?
2. What current local public-health, healthcare, shelter, school/workplace, or facility instructions apply?
3. Who is sick or exposed, and can they reduce close contact without creating a worse immediate danger?
4. Does the current place have crowding, poor air, sanitation problems, unsafe water/food, power loss, heat/cold exposure, violence, or blocked exits?
5. What communication, records, medicines, devices, caregivers, pets/service animals, and transport are needed before changing shelter or route?

## Do Now

- Put life-threatening illness, worsening symptoms, serious injury, heat/cold exposure, violence, fire, gas, CO, floodwater, chemical, or radiation danger through the Emergency Front Door first.
- Follow current local public-health and healthcare instructions; use official local sources for shelter, school/workplace, testing, treatment, vaccination, and return-to-activity rules.
- If someone is sick, reduce close contact when possible, keep basic needs close, protect higher-risk people, and route healthcare access for severe, worsening, or high-risk cases.
- Use layered prevention as routing, not as a magic shield: hygiene, cleaner air where possible, staying home/away from others when sick, and masks or distance as bounded added layers when appropriate.
- Keep medicines, medical devices, chargers, assistive equipment, records, contacts, and caregiver support close if safe.
- In shelters, facilities, aid points, and transport, balance disease risk with exposure, water/food, sanitation, accessibility, safety, family separation, and official instructions.
- If public-health messages conflict or look false, use Card 13 without delaying emergency care or escape from direct danger.

## Do Not

- Do not diagnose the disease, estimate incubation, decide contagiousness, or identify the pathogen from symptoms.
- Do not give treatment protocols, medication choices, doses, vaccine schedules, testing procedures, or quarantine-law advice from this card.
- Do not hide severe illness, falsify records, evade public-health checks, or spread rumors.
- Do not separate children, disabled people, medically dependent people, or caregivers unless a current safety route supports it.
- Do not treat masks, open windows, filters, improvised barriers, or a crowded facility as proof of safety.
- Do not repair HVAC, redesign ventilation, build filters, run medical equipment unsafely, or ignore CO/fire/electrical hazards for cleaner air.
- Do not turn public-health uncertainty into anti-authority, legal, protest, enforcement, or conflict tactics.

## Route By Problem

| Problem | Go now |
| --- | --- |
| Severe or worsening illness, high-risk person, medicine/device need, pregnancy, infant/child, disability, older adult, pet/service animal care | `07_FIRST_AID_AND_HEALTH_CONTINUITY.md` and healthcare/public-health routes |
| Current public-health order, exposure notice, shelter/facility outbreak, sick household, or epidemic/pandemic instruction | `01_EMERGENCY_FRONT_DOOR.md`; then this card and current local public-health instructions |
| Missing, stale, conflicting, impersonated, impossible, or visibly unsafe public-health instruction, false all-clear, suspicious worker, rumor, or official-looking demand | `hazard_cards/13_CONFLICTING_UNRELIABLE_INSTRUCTIONS.md`; then return here for disease-risk routing |
| Crowded shelter, shared air, unsafe shelter, evacuation, transport, movement, or facility access | `08_EXPOSURE_SHELTER_WEATHER_MOVEMENT.md`, this card, and official/local instructions |
| Water, food, hand hygiene, sanitation, medicine storage, cleaning supplies, or contaminated supplies | `05_WATER_HYGIENE_FOOD_MINIMUMS.md` |
| Power outage affecting devices, refrigeration, heat/cold, cleaner air, communications, or CO/generator risk | `06_FIRE_POWER_UTILITIES_CO.md` |
| Panic, stigma, separation, rumor stress, overloaded helpers, crowd stress | `10_PSYCHOLOGICAL_FIRST_AID_GROUP_STRESS.md` and `09_PROTECT_YOURSELF.md` |
| Alerts, public-health updates, contacts, records, assistance, reunification, route status | `12_COMMUNICATION_ALERTS_RECORDS_NAVIGATION.md` |
| Re-entry, facility reopening, aid-point access, documentation, or cleanup pressure during illness/crowding | `11_CLEANUP_REENTRY_EARLY_RECOVERY.md` and current public-health guidance |

## Sick Or Exposed Boundary

If someone is sick or exposed, the first route is not disease identification. Reduce unnecessary close contact when possible, protect higher-risk people, keep needed supplies close, and get healthcare/public-health guidance for severe, worsening, or high-risk cases.

If reducing contact would create a worse danger, such as leaving a child alone, losing medical-device support, entering heat/cold exposure, crossing floodwater, entering violence, or missing emergency care, route that direct danger first.

## Shelter, Facility, And Crowd Boundary

A stocked facility is not automatically safe during a contagious-disease event. Check crowding, exits, sanitation, water/food, air, medicine/device support, caregiver access, discrimination/social tension, security, and official closure or public-health status before relying on it.

This card does not teach shelter outbreak management, healthcare infection-control, school/work policy, workplace policy, or facility law.

## Card 13 Reliability Boundary

Use Card 13 only when public-health instructions are missing, stale, conflicting, impersonated, impossible, or visibly unsafe. If instructions are current, local, specific, verifiable, and not contradicted by direct physical danger, follow them and monitor updates.

Card 13 is reliability-seeking. It is not an excuse for evasion, forged records, hiding illness, harassment, confrontation, legal advice, or anti-authority tactics.

## R-D-E And Tier Notes

- Biological/pandemic hazards can lower `E` through crowding, shared air, poor sanitation, unsafe shelter, lack of medical care, and exposure around higher-risk people.
- Biological/pandemic hazards can lower `R` if medicine, devices, caregivers, transport, safe shelter, water, food, communication, or trusted healthcare access are disrupted.
- Biological/pandemic hazards can raise `D` when public health, hospitals, shelters, schools/workplaces, transport, supply chains, and official information are strained together.
- Tier 0: severe/worsening illness, high-risk person without care, active public-health order affecting movement/shelter, unsafe crowd/shelter, or loss of medical/device support.
- Tier 1 and Tier 2: sick/exposed routing, hygiene, cleaner-air choices, medicine/device continuity, public-health updates, shelter/crowd decisions, and records/contact rhythm.
- Tier 3 and Tier 4: public-health systems, healthcare capacity, vaccination/testing programs, surveillance, WASH depth, shelter operations, labor/school continuity, and community governance stubs.

## Stubbed For Later

Later packets must handle respiratory pandemic depth, foodborne/waterborne outbreaks, vector-borne disease, zoonotic disease, shelter/facility outbreak management, vaccination/testing routing, healthcare capacity, long-term public-health governance, and WASH disease-control depth. This card only routes first decisions.

## Smoke-Test Checks

| Scenario | Expected first route |
| --- | --- |
| `R5-D4-E5 URBAN UNREST EPIDEMIC` | Route public-health instructions, crowd pressure, facility safety, sanitation, communication, personal safety, and Card 13 only if reliability breaks. |
| `R3-D2-E3 SICK HOUSEHOLD POWER OUTAGE` | Route illness, vulnerable people, medicine/device continuity, food/water, safe heat/cooling, CO, and contacts together. |
| `R4-D3-E2 SHELTER RESPIRATORY OUTBREAK` | Use public-health instructions, hygiene, cleaner air where possible, masks/distance as bounded layers, vulnerable-person checks, and group-stress routing. |
| `R5-D4-E5 FACILITY EPIDEMIC CROWDING` | Facility resources are not usable until crowding, sanitation, air, exits, official status, and vulnerable-person access are safe enough. |
| `R3-D2-E3 CONFLICTING PUBLIC HEALTH MESSAGES FAMILY` | Use current local public-health sources first; if reliability breaks, route to Card 13 without turning the card anti-authority. |
| `R5-D4-E5 FACILITY FALSE ALL-CLEAR` | Visible illness/crowding hazards, public-health status, facility closure, sanitation, air, and exits route before facility-resource use. |
| Flood re-entry with illness/crowding at aid point | Floodwater and re-entry hazards still win; then route aid-point crowding, hygiene, higher-risk people, and public-health instructions. |

## Scope

Use this chapter when someone is hurt, may be choking, has severe bleeding, has burns/smoke exposure, has lightning-strike injury, has hurricane/tsunami/flood/wind injury, has chemical exposure, may be radiologically contaminated, has severe or worsening illness, is sick/exposed during a contagious-disease event, has a disaster wound, is trapped or unable to move safely, or depends on medicine, medical devices, care support, infant/child supplies, pregnancy/postpartum care, mobility aids, communication aids, service animals, or pets.

This chapter is not a complete first-aid course. It does not teach CPR, infant choking, tourniquet placement, wound packing, diagnosis, disease identification, medication dosing, treatment protocols, vaccine schedules, poisoning treatment, lightning-strike treatment, chemical-burn treatment, radiation-sickness treatment, KI dosing, decontamination procedure, device repair, childbirth, formula preparation, or pet first aid.

## First Aid First Pass

Check in this order:

1. Is the scene safe enough to help?
2. Is there severe bleeding?
3. Can the person breathe, speak, cry, or cough effectively?
4. Is the person unresponsive, badly burned, smoke-exposed, crushed, shocked, or unable to move safely?
5. Are wounds contaminated by floodwater, standing water, debris, bites, punctures, or chemicals?
6. Does the person have a medical dependency that will fail without medicine, power, refrigeration, mobility, communication, or caregiver support?

Get emergency or trained help when available.

If emergency or trained help is unavailable, unreachable, overloaded, or unsafe, do not turn this chapter into improvised medical care. Route life threats and active hazards first, preserve communication and records, protect medicines/devices, use alternate contact paths when available, and seek safer shelter or transport toward reachable care only when that is safer than staying.

## Severe Bleeding

If bleeding appears life-threatening, apply firm direct pressure with the cleanest available material and keep pressure on while seeking help.

If trained and equipped, use bleeding-control tools according to that training. Do not improvise detailed procedures from memory or from this skeleton.

## Choking Or Airway Danger

If a person cannot breathe, speak, cry, or cough effectively, treat it as an immediate emergency and get help.

If the person can cough forcefully or speak, monitor closely and do not interfere with that effective coughing. Detailed adult/child/infant choking procedures need a dedicated reviewed card.

## Wounds After Disaster

Keep wounds as clean and covered as possible. Keep them away from floodwater or standing water.

Seek medical help when available for wounds that are dirty, deep, puncture wounds, bites, crushed injuries, infected-looking, flood-contaminated, or hard to clean.

## Burns And Smoke Exposure

For thermal burns, cool the burn promptly with cool or cold potable water when available. Remove rings, jewelry, belts, or tight items near the burned area before swelling.

Loosely cover while waiting for care. Escalate burns involving the face, hands, feet, genitals, large areas, children, or any sign of smoke inhalation.

## Health Continuity Checks

Ask early:

- Who needs prescription medicine, refrigerated medicine, oxygen, powered devices, mobility aids, hearing/vision/communication aids, caregiver support, or special transport?
- Who is pregnant, postpartum, breastfeeding, an infant, a child, older adult, disabled, medically fragile, or unable to communicate symptoms clearly?
- What supplies, records, chargers, batteries, documents, device information, feeding supplies, diapers, water, and sanitation items must move with them?
- Are service animals or pets present, and what food, water, medicines, leash/carrier, waste supplies, and records do they need?

## Medicine, Devices, And Power

Protect prescription information, medical documents, device information, chargers, batteries, and critical supplies.

If medicine or a device depends on power or cold storage, prioritize official charging/cooling locations, pharmacies, providers, shelters, emergency services, or evacuation before it fails.

EPAP may help eligible uninsured people replace prescriptions, supplies, vaccines, and some equipment when activated for the disaster area. It is not automatic coverage and does not replace planning.

## Do Not

- Do not change medication doses, substitute medicine, ration critical medicine, or stop medicine based on this manual.
- Do not repair medical devices, wire batteries, or improvise oxygen/device systems from this chapter.
- Do not prepare formula, childbirth care, infant choking care, or pet medical care from this skeleton.
- Do not close wounds, suture, remove deeply embedded objects, or delay professional care for serious injury.

## Routing

| Finding | Route |

| Severe bleeding, airway danger, unresponsive person, serious burns | Emergency services/trained help first; this chapter only supports first recognition. |
| Wound exposed to floodwater/debris | This chapter plus `hazard_cards/01_FLOOD.md` and `11_CLEANUP_REENTRY_EARLY_RECOVERY.md`. |
| Suspected heat illness, inability to cool down, confusion, fainting, collapse | This chapter plus `hazard_cards/02_HEAT.md`; emergency/trained help when available. |
| Suspected hypothermia, frostbite, serious cold exposure, or inability to get warm | This chapter plus `hazard_cards/03_COLD.md`; emergency/trained help when available. |
| Wildfire smoke exposure, new/worsening breathing or chest symptoms, asthma/COPD/heart risk, pregnancy, children, older adults | This chapter plus `hazard_cards/04_WILDFIRE_SMOKE.md`; emergency/trained help when available. |
| Earthquake injury, trapped person, burn/smoke exposure, contaminated wound, crush concern, or inability to move safely | This chapter plus `hazard_cards/05_EARTHQUAKE.md`; emergency/trained help when available. |
| Tornado/severe-wind injury, trapped person, wound, puncture, serious bleeding, smoke/dust exposure, or inability to move safely | This chapter plus `hazard_cards/06_TORNADO_SEVERE_WIND.md`; emergency/trained help when available. |
| Lightning strike, collapse, fall, burn, breathing/cardiac concern, or injury while moving from thunderstorm danger | This chapter plus `hazard_cards/09_LIGHTNING.md`; emergency/trained help when available. This chapter does not teach CPR procedure depth. |
| Hurricane/tropical-storm injury, floodwater wound, debris/glass injury, CO concern, medicine/device disruption, evacuation shelter health need, or re-entry injury | This chapter plus `hazard_cards/10_HURRICANE.md`; emergency/trained help when available. This chapter does not teach medical or cleanup procedure depth. |
| Tsunami/coastal flood injury, floodwater wound, debris injury, drowning concern, evacuation health need, medicine/device disruption, or re-entry injury | This chapter plus `hazard_cards/11_TSUNAMI_COASTAL.md`; emergency/trained help when available. This chapter does not teach drowning treatment, medical procedure depth, rescue, or cleanup. |
| Chemical exposure, suspected poisoning, ingestion, breathing trouble, eye/skin/throat irritation, contaminated wound, or inability to get clean | This chapter plus `hazard_cards/07_CHEMICAL_HAZMAT.md`; Poison Control, 911, hospital/medical help, or veterinary help when available. |
| Radiation/nuclear alert with burns, injuries, possible contamination, contaminated wounds, breathing trouble, medicine/device needs, KI rumor, or inability to move safely | This chapter plus `hazard_cards/08_RADIATION_NUCLEAR.md`; trained/medical, public-health, or official screening help when available. |
| Severe or worsening illness, sick/exposed household, shelter/facility outbreak, high-risk sick person, public-health instruction, or medicine/device continuity during contagious disease | This chapter plus `hazard_cards/12_BIOLOGICAL_PANDEMIC_CONTAGIOUS_DISEASE.md`; healthcare/public-health routes when available. This chapter does not diagnose disease or give treatment protocols. |
| Power-dependent medical device or refrigerated medicine | This chapter plus `06_FIRE_POWER_UTILITIES_CO.md`. |
| Emergency services, Poison Control, clinic/hospital, pharmacy, public-health line, dialysis/device support, shelter medical support, or trained help unavailable, unreachable, overloaded, or unsafe | Route immediate life threats and active hazards first; use `12_COMMUNICATION_ALERTS_RECORDS_NAVIGATION.md` for short messages and alternate channels, preserve medicine/device/provider records, seek reachable care only when movement is safer than staying, and use `hazard_cards/13_CONFLICTING_UNRELIABLE_INSTRUCTIONS.md` if reliability or impersonation is the issue. |
| Missing, stale, conflicting, impersonated, impossible, or visibly unsafe medical, shelter, aid, screening, KI, Poison Control, or official-looking help instructions | `hazard_cards/13_CONFLICTING_UNRELIABLE_INSTRUCTIONS.md`; route life-threatening injury, exposure, chemical, or radiation danger first. |
| Infant feeding, pregnancy/postpartum, child health | This chapter now; dedicated source packets later before detail. |
| Stress, panic, group shock after injury | `10_PSYCHOLOGICAL_FIRST_AID_GROUP_STRESS.md`. |

## Smoke-Test Checks

| Scenario | This chapter should force |
|---|---|
| `R1-D1-E1 HOT DESERT ALONE` | Immediate bleeding/airway/burn check, then heat card, exposure/water/self-rescue. |
| `R3-D2-E3 COLD POWER-OUT CHILDREN` | Cold card, children, medicines/devices, CO/smoke exposure, burns, choking, and safe heat routing. |

| Flood re-entry | Flood card route, wound contamination, electrical injury risk, medicine/device contamination, and cleanup/re-entry stub. |
| `R4-D3-E2 WILDFIRE SMOKE ASTHMA` | Smoke card route, high-risk breathing check, medicines/devices, cleaner-air route, and early trained-help escalation. |
| `R3-D3-E2 EARTHQUAKE APARTMENT GAS SMELL` | Earthquake and utility routes first; injuries, smoke exposure, trapped people, medicine/device needs, and stress route here after the scene is safer. |
| `R5-D4-E5 URBAN FACILITY AFTERSHOCKS` | Injury recognition, trapped/separated people, medicine/device continuity, group logs, and trained-help routing without rescue or medical procedure depth. |
| `R3-D3-E2 TORNADO WARNING MOBILE HOME` | Shelter-now route first; injuries, trapped people, wounds, medicine/device needs, and stress route here after immediate wind danger is safer. |
| `R2-D2-E1 DRIVING SEVERE THUNDERSTORM` | Vehicle/wind route first; injuries from crash, debris, downed lines, or glass route here without medical procedure depth. |
| `R5-D3-E4 FACILITY SEVERE WIND DOWNED LINES` | Injury recognition, trapped/separated people, medicine/device continuity, and trained-help routing while avoiding downed-line and damaged-building hazards. |
| `R4-D3-E2 CHEMICAL RELEASE SHELTER-IN-PLACE` | Chemical card first; exposure symptoms, ingestion, inability to get clean, medicines/devices, and vulnerable people route here without poisoning-treatment detail. |
| `R5-D4-E5 FACILITY CHEMICAL ODOR` | Chemical card first; treat breathing/eye/skin/throat symptoms, exposure, and medical dependencies as trained-help routes, not facility self-treatment. |
| `R3-D3-E3 KI RUMOR CHILDREN` | Radiation card first; do not self-dose, follow current public-health instructions, and route child/medicine/device concerns here without KI dosing or treatment detail. |
| `R2-D2-E1 OPEN FIELD THUNDER` | Lightning card first; route strike injury, fall injury, burns, breathing/cardiac concern, and exposed movement here only after scene safety is improving. |
| `R4-D3-E2 OUTDOOR GROUP LIGHTNING` | Lightning card first; account for separated/injured people, use trained-help routes, and avoid CPR or medical procedure detail in this volume. |
| `R2-D2-E1 BOAT LIGHTNING` | Lightning card first; open-water danger and emergency/local instructions come before ordinary first-aid routing. |
| `R3-D3-E2 HURRICANE EVACUATION ORDER FAMILY` | Hurricane card first; medicines, devices, children, pregnancy/disability needs, pets/service animals, and evacuation shelter health needs route here without delaying the order. |

| `R3-D3-E2 COASTAL EARTHQUAKE TSUNAMI WARNING FAMILY` | Earthquake then tsunami/coastal cards first; medicines, devices, children, pregnancy/disability needs, pets/service animals, and evacuation health needs route here without delaying movement. |
| `R2-D2-E1 BEACH LONG EARTHQUAKE` | Earthquake and tsunami/coastal routes first; injuries, floodwater exposure, drowning concern, and mobility limits route here only after scene safety improves. |
| `R3-D2-E3 AFTER TSUNAMI HOME REENTRY CHILDREN` | Tsunami/coastal and re-entry routes first; floodwater wounds, debris injuries, medicines/devices, children, and stress route here without cleanup or medical procedure depth. |
| `R3-D2-E3 SICK HOUSEHOLD POWER OUTAGE` | Biological/pandemic and utility routes first; illness, higher-risk people, medicines/devices, safe heat/cooling, food/water, CO, and healthcare contact route here without diagnosis or treatment depth. |
| `R4-D3-E2 SHELTER RESPIRATORY OUTBREAK` | Biological/pandemic route first; shelter health needs, higher-risk people, medicines/devices, hygiene, and trained/public-health help route here without infection-control procedure depth. |
| `R3-D2-E3 SICK HOUSEHOLD 911 BUSY` | Route severe/worsening illness and contagious-disease risk first; use alternate contact paths and short location/condition/need messages without diagnosis or treatment protocols. |
| `R3-D2-E3 CHILD FEVER CLINIC CLOSED` | Protect the child from exposure/dehydration risks, preserve medicine/provider records, seek reachable care or public-health/provider routes, and do not add fever dosing advice here. |
| `R4-D3-E2 SHELTER MEDICAL DESK OVERLOADED` | Keep group logs and privacy, identify high-risk dependencies, use alternate official care channels, and do not turn the shelter into an unreviewed clinic. |
| `R3-D3-E2 POWER OUTAGE OXYGEN DEVICE` | Route utility/CO/power danger first; preserve device info, seek backup power/shelter/provider/emergency routes before failure, and do not repair or rewire equipment. |
| `R2-D2-E1 POISON CONTROL PHONE FAILURE` | Route chemical/poison hazard first, try Poison Help/911/alternate official channels when reachable, and do not provide poisoning treatment from this chapter. |
| `R5-D4-E5 FACILITY EPIDEMIC HOSPITAL DIVERSION` | Use biological/pandemic routing plus records, medical dependencies, privacy, communication, and movement toward reachable care when safer than staying. |
| Flood re-entry with contaminated medicines and unreachable pharmacy | Flood and re-entry hazards block retrieval; preserve records, use FDA medicine-safety boundaries, and seek replacement/provider/pharmacy routes only when safe. |

| Tier 2: Medium | Partial coverage through routines, logs, roles, and safety boundaries. | Systems for water, sanitation, energy, food, medicine, shelter, security, records. |
| Tier 3: Critical | Routing only. | Community reconstruction and infrastructure triage. |
| Tier 4: Reconstruction | Routing only. | The 101-node rebuild graph and later civilization-rebuild volumes. |

## Later Source Review Packets

Do not draft final operational chapters for these until a matching review packet exists:

- degraded medical help / dead endpoints packet exists for routing boundaries when 911, Poison Control, hospitals/clinics, pharmacies, public-health lines, dialysis/device support, shelter medical desks, charging/cooling locations, official routes, or trained help are unavailable, unreachable, overloaded, impossible, or unsafe; later work must review any mini-card, medication/device continuity depth, CPR/AED/choking, or healthcare-scarcity guidance separately;
- hazard cards: flood, heat, cold, wildfire smoke, earthquake, tornado/severe wind, chemical/hazmat, radiation/nuclear, lightning, hurricane, tsunami/coastal, biological/pandemic/contagious disease, and missing/stale/conflicting instructions exist; use `notes/HAZARD_CARD_FORMAT_GUIDE.md` and `manual/volume_01/hazard_cards/_HAZARD_CARD_TEMPLATE.md` for the next card; the degraded medical help / dead endpoints packet now exists as routing support, so next work should decide whether it needs a mini-card or move to source indexing;
- deeper WASH: water treatment, storage, sanitation, latrines, waste, facility hygiene;
- food systems: safe storage, cooking, gardens, preservation, livestock, foraging safety;
- field survival: shelter, fire, signaling, desert/cold/wet/open-water environments;
- medical/public health: CPR, bleeding control depth, infection control, medications, childbirth, chronic illness, epidemiology;
- utilities/repair: electrical, gas, fuel, generators, water systems, tools, mechanical repair;
- cleanup/rebuilding: mold, sewage, debris, ash/smoke, structural safety, housing repair;
- communications/navigation: radio legality, maps, compass, offline data, community messages;
- governance and ethics: conflict mediation, access control, rationing, records, rights, vulnerable-person protection;
- reconstruction graph: materials, energy, agriculture, manufacturing, education, law, science, and infrastructure.

## Source-Review Rule

The durable process remains:

1. Pick one narrow packet.
2. Inventory sources.
3. Summarize agreement and conflicts.
4. Flag safety-sensitive claims.
5. List claims allowed and not allowed.
6. Map to `R-D-E`, tiers, and later graph nodes.
7. Draft only the matching chapter surface.
8. Run smoke scenarios and safety scan.

This keeps the manual from becoming a pile of interesting but unsafe facts.

Future hazard cards should also follow `notes/HAZARD_CARD_FORMAT_GUIDE.md`. Only reviewed numbered cards matching `manual/volume_01/hazard_cards/[0-9][0-9]_*.md` belong in the assembled review copy.

This chapter is the minimum layer for the first 48 hours. Full water and sanitation methods stay in deeper reviewed chapters.

## Water

Use water in this priority order:

1. Sealed commercial bottled water.
2. Water that local authorities say is safe.
3. Water made safe for germs by a reviewed method.
4. Untreated unknown water only when dehydration is the greater immediate danger, and then route to water treatment as soon as possible.

If safe tap water is uncertain, use bottled, boiled, or treated water for:

- drinking;
- cooking;
- brushing teeth;
- infant-care tasks;
- basic hygiene.

Boiling is the preferred simple method for germs when the water is not chemically contaminated. Cloudy water should be settled or filtered first. Clear water should reach a rolling boil for 1 minute, or 3 minutes above 6,500 feet, then cool and be stored covered in clean sanitized containers.

Do not rely on boiling or disinfection for water that may contain fuel, toxic chemicals, or radioactive material. If a chemical/hazmat alert, unknown powder/liquid, chemical odor, or suspected exposure affects water, food, medicine, containers, or wounds, route first to `hazard_cards/07_CHEMICAL_HAZMAT.md`. If a radiation/fallout alert, radiological-contamination warning, uncovered outdoor food/water, or KI rumor affects food, water, medicine, containers, or wounds, route first to `hazard_cards/08_RADIATION_NUCLEAR.md`.

## Containers

Use food-grade containers when possible. Do not use containers that held toxic chemicals such as bleach or pesticides for drinking water.

Keep drinking water away from:

- fuel;
- pesticides;
- sewage and diapers;
- animal waste;
- trash;
- floodwater;
- direct heat and sunlight when avoidable.

## Hygiene And Sanitation

The first sanitation job is separation:

- feces away from hands;
- hands away from drinking water;
- waste away from food;
- animals away from water and food;
- fuel and chemicals away from everything people drink or eat.

Wash hands with soap and safe water when available, especially after toilet/waste contact and before food, water handling, or infant care.

If normal toilets do not work, do not let waste contaminate the water source, food area, sleeping area, or handwashing area. Detailed emergency toilet and latrine methods need a later sanitation review.

## Food

During a power outage:

- keep refrigerator and freezer doors closed;
- treat a closed refrigerator as roughly a 4-hour cold buffer;
- treat a full closed freezer as roughly a 48-hour cold buffer;
- treat a half-full closed freezer as roughly a 24-hour cold buffer.

Never taste food to decide whether it is safe.

Discard perishable food that has been above 40 F for 2 hours or more, or 1 hour if temperatures are above 90 F.

Do not eat food that contacted floodwater unless a later reviewed food-safety source explicitly allows cleaning and sanitizing that exact sealed container type.

If the main issue is active flooding, floodwater around a building, or floodwater touching food, water, medicine, wounds, utilities, or records, route first to `hazard_cards/01_FLOOD.md`.

If heat is spoiling food, increasing water need, damaging medicine, or making hygiene harder, route first to `hazard_cards/02_HEAT.md`. If cold is freezing water, damaging supplies, or paired with a power outage, route first to `hazard_cards/03_COLD.md`.

If wildfire smoke, ash, evacuation, heat/smoke conflict, or power loss is affecting food, water, medicine, hygiene, pets, or records, route first to `hazard_cards/04_WILDFIRE_SMOKE.md` and then return here for minimum water/food decisions.

If tornado/severe wind, stormwater, damaged shelter, downed lines, outage, broken glass/debris, or official shelter movement affects food, water, medicine, hygiene, pets, or records, route first to `hazard_cards/06_TORNADO_SEVERE_WIND.md` and then return here for minimum water/food decisions.

If hurricane/tropical-storm alerts, storm surge, floodwater, outage, evacuation, sheltering, re-entry, damaged buildings, downed lines, or official return instructions affect food, water, medicine, hygiene, pets, or records, route first to `hazard_cards/10_HURRICANE.md` and `hazard_cards/01_FLOOD.md` as needed, then return here for minimum water/food decisions.

If tsunami warning signs, official tsunami alerts, coastal evacuation, floodwater, outage, re-entry, damaged buildings, downed lines, beach/harbor/waterway danger, or official return instructions affect food, water, medicine, hygiene, pets, or records, route first to `hazard_cards/11_TSUNAMI_COASTAL.md` and `hazard_cards/01_FLOOD.md` as needed, then return here for minimum water/food decisions.

If chemical/hazmat release, exposure, unknown residue, contaminated air, household chemicals, or official chemical shelter/evacuation instructions affect food, water, medicine, hygiene, pets, or records, route first to `hazard_cards/07_CHEMICAL_HAZMAT.md` and then return here for minimum water/food decisions.

If radiation/nuclear alert, fallout warning, radiological contamination, uncovered outdoor food/water, contaminated clothing/belongings, or official get-inside/stay-inside/all-clear instructions affect food, water, medicine, hygiene, pets, or records, route first to `hazard_cards/08_RADIATION_NUCLEAR.md` and then return here only for allowed minimum water/food decisions.

If contagious-disease instructions, sick/exposed people, shelter/facility outbreak, epidemic/pandemic crowding, shared sanitation, shared air, aid-point crowding, or public-health return/activity rules affect water, food, hygiene, medicine, or shelter choice, route first to `hazard_cards/12_BIOLOGICAL_PANDEMIC_CONTAGIOUS_DISEASE.md` and then return here for minimum water/food decisions.

If water, food, medicine, shelter, return, aid, or all-clear instructions are missing, stale, conflicting, impersonated, impossible, or visibly unsafe, route through `hazard_cards/13_CONFLICTING_UNRELIABLE_INSTRUCTIONS.md` after controlling any direct contamination, flood, chemical, or radiation hazard.

## Group WASH Stub

For groups, the minimum routine is:

- identify drinking water;
- identify handwashing water;
- separate toilets/waste from water and food;
- keep soap or hygiene substitutes visible;
- assign someone to check water, waste, and food hazards daily.

Settlement-level sanitation, wells, wastewater, drainage, vector control, and hygiene promotion require later WASH source reviews.

# Water, Hygiene, And Food Minimums

Pilot SSOT node for minimum safe-life checks on hydration, sanitation separation,
and short-duration food safety.

Core routing intent:

- Use this node after immediate-danger handling when the immediate threat map includes
  water contamination, hygiene breakdown, or spoiled food risk.
- Defer detailed engineering or treatment recipes to later reviewed packets.
